references.text: God promises Abram to make him a great nation and bless him – an early promise later expanded in Gen 17:4 to include that Abraham will become the father of many nations.
God promises Abram descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, further elaborated in Gen 17:4 with the promise of many nations.
God gives Abram the new name Abraham ('father of a multitude') and expands the promise by declaring that nations and kings will come from him.

God renews His promise to Abraham regarding numerous descendants and that all the families of the earth will be blessed through his offspring, paralleling the promise to be the father of many nations.
Paul directly quotes Gen 17:5 and confirms that Abraham was made 'the father of many nations' by virtue of his faith in God who gives life to the dead.
Paul describes Abraham as the father of all who believe, both circumcised and uncircumcised, as the fulfillment of the promise to be the father of many nations.

Paul writes that those who belong to Christ are Abraham's offspring and heirs according to the promise, showing the spiritual fulfillment of the promise that Abraham would be the father of many nations.
Direct retelling of the same covenant promise to become a multitude of nations, given to Jacob as the fulfillment of Abraham's calling.
Paul quoted this promise directly to support the teaching that faith, not the law, makes one an heir of the promise of many nations.
Direct continuation of the same covenant in the same chapter; defines the sign and obligation linked to the promise of many nations.
Direct confirmation of Abraham's covenant with Isaac, containing the same promises of numerous descendants and blessing for all nations.
The first retelling of the promise later specified in 17:4; shows the development from 'a great nation' to 'a multitude of nations'.
Same chapter; shows that the promise of abundance also applies to Ishmael, even though the eternal covenant is linked to Isaac.
Quoted Abraham's covenant to show that believers (including Gentiles) are heirs to the promise that all families will be blessed.
Direct continuation in the same chapter; confirms that Sarah too will become a nation, expanding and confirming the promise in verse 4.
Remembering Abraham's covenant that applies to 'thousands of generations,' confirming that the promise of many nations is eternal.
Identical with Psalm 105:8; confirms that God's covenant and promise regarding many generations is eternal.
